correction.text: Fars, the Salghurid atabegate (Shiraz and the province)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Salghurids). 'The Salghurids were established by Sunqur in 1148'; they are the Atabegs of Fars, capital Shiraz. The page gives no area and no frontier; Fars is drawn as the historical Persis region. The brief occupation of Isfahan (1203-4) and the Bahrain occupation are hatched ledger events, not territory.

union.text: Fars, the Salghurid atabegate (Shiraz and the province)
Kish Island, with its dues on Persian Gulf-India trade

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Abu Bakr 'captured' Kish Island on 12 November 1230, 'which gave him control over dues on Persian Gulf-India trade' (Abu Bakr ibn Sa'd page). Fars stays the same until 1282. Vassal of the Seljuks, then the Khwarazm Shahs under Sa'd I, then the Mongols (from Abu Bakr's allegiance to Hulagu and Sa'd II's mission to Baghdad): suzerains' tints, not drawn here.

region.text: Fars, the Salghurid atabegate (Shiraz and the province)

ledger.note: 1148: Sunqur founds the Salghurid atabegate of Fars at Shiraz. 'The Salghurids were established by Sunqur in 1148, who had profited from the rebellions during the reign of' Sultan Mas'ud; infobox 'Established: 1148'. The page names Fars (Atabegs of Fars), not its limits.

ledger.counterpart: holder of Isfahan (not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1203: the Salghurids briefly occupy Isfahan. 'They briefly occupied Isfahan in 1203-4.' The page does not name the holder.

ledger.counterpart: holder of Isfahan (not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1204: the Isfahan occupation ends ('1203-4'); the page does not say how.

region.text: Kish Island, with its dues on Persian Gulf-India trade

ledger.counterpart: Kish (ruler not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1230: Abu Bakr takes Kish Island on 12 November, 'which gave him control over dues on Persian Gulf-India trade'.

1236: the Salghurids seize the islands of Bahrain in August, 'officially part of the Abbasid Caliphate' (Abu Bakr page); the Salghurids page says they 'occupied Bahrain, which they took from the Uyunid dynasty in 1235'. The Uyunid page opened has no word of the Salghurids.
1253: end of the occupation, at confidence 1: no page opened says when the Salghurids left Bahrain; the Uyunid page's only dated event is its fall 'to the Usfurids of Banu Uqayl in 651 AH (1253 CE)'.

zones.text: Fars, the Salghurid atabegate (Shiraz and the province)

wars.outcome: After Hulagu occupied northern Iran and Baghdad, Abu Bakr declared allegiance by sending his son Sa'd II; Saljuq Shah rebelled and was captured and executed in 1264, when Hulagu had Abish Khatun declared atabeg; a revolt of 1265 was suppressed. Fars was ruled directly by the Ilkhanate after the end of the line.
wars.note: Dates from the Abish Khatun page; the Abu Bakr page gives the allegiance without a year.

certainty.note: Fars as a province; no frontier on the pages opened. Kish Island is a point holding. The Bahrain and Isfahan occupations are hatched and approximate.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Four pages opened. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Disagreements: Bahrain taken 1235 (Salghurids page, 'from the Uyunid dynasty') vs August 1236 (Abu Bakr page); end of line 1282 (infobox) vs Abish Khatun's removal in 1284 and death 1285/86; Abish's reign 1263-1284 (list) vs 1264-1282 (infobox).
Not settled: when the Salghurid hold on Bahrain ended (confidence 1 at 1253); who held Isfahan in 1203; the Eldiguzid forcing of the Salghurid atabeg to submit (Eldiguz page, undated); Salghurid involvement in the succession of the Kerman Seljuks (no dates). The Salghurids were vassals of the Seljuks, then 'for the Khwarazm Shahs in the 13th century' (Sa'd I acknowledged them), then of the Mongols; none of these is dated on a page here, and they belong to the suzerains' dossiers (great-seljuk-empire, khwarezmid-empire, ulus-of-hulegu).
Fars is drawn as the gazetteer's 'Persis' region (about 157,000 km2), which includes the Gulf coast near Bushehr; the page gives no extent. 'Kish' is a place the gazetteer lacks.
Counterpart note: the uyunid-emirate dossier's own 1253 dissolve cites the Usfurids and the 1235 Salghurid invasion; it carries no event mirroring this occupation.
